solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rescue vessel, if able to, at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat sent out to rescue people, so long as it can make the trip on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the nautical picture but is the anagram signal: the letters of IF ABLE TO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is the craft launched to save people in trouble on the water.

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits beneath, so the shop word goes on top

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Factory

explanation.surface: A factory's top levels are held up by the retail floor below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' in a down answer means the Y from 'Factory ultimately' sits below STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, the same idea as a floor.

parts.note: re is a standard word for about or concerning
an MP is a Member of Parliament, so a member

explanation.surface: Telling old stories about a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past times, which is what remembering does.

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word designer

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A fashion designer at last receives an official award.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment, and to dress someone can be to robe them.

indicators.note: heard says the solver must go by how the girl's name is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's pet name is overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: MONICA, said out loud, gives the less common spelling of moniker.
explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is an informal name, the sort of label a nickname is.

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the word stream is rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher in charge of the weak class or set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stream' looks like a school ability group, but its letters are rearranged after the signal 'poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Master is an old-fashioned title for a schoolteacher, as in schoolmaster.

indicators.note: being short means lacking the last bit, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: an event is a happening

explanation.surface: School clothing that turns out to be too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be short' drops the final T from EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and uniform both describe something level and consistent throughout.

indicators.note: outside says the pen word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes

indicators.note: extremely takes the two end letters of the word smart

explanation.surface: An author sits outside a very fashionable eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen: Biro is a British brand name used for any ballpoint pen. 'outside' wraps it around the ends of 'smart'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

indicators.note: in says the one-and-female letters go inside the group word

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians or people
I is the Roman numeral one
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman is thrown out of a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to send them away, so banished means expelled.

clue.text: Attention needed after weight put on

indicators.note: needed after says the attention letters follow the weight letter

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Someone must watch it after piling on the pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like gaining weight; it is the definition, as in putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear clothes is to have them put on.

clue.text: Signal given by copper close to scene

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the last letter of scene

explanation.surface: A police officer near a crime scene makes a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt or signal telling someone to act or speak.

parts.note: a copy is an imitation
a volume is a book

explanation.surface: A fake book appears in the display.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook as an adjective means exemplary or flawless, like the model writing in an exercise book.

clue.text: Witness waiter, perhaps, supporting old boy

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes below, so the waiter word sits under the old boy

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a waiter is one example of a server

explanation.surface: A witness at a restaurant: the waiter, helping out a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is someone who observes an event, an observer.

clue.text: Belly laugh coming from muscular oarsman

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A burly rower lets out a loud guffaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar of laughter is a loud, hearty laugh from deep in the chest.

parts.note: a version is one account or reading of something

explanation.surface: Someone takes against one reading of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike for something.

clue.text: Piece of information I came across in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them, so met

explanation.surface: A fact someone stumbled on after giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but 'in retirement' signals the meeting word reads backwards after I.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single entry or snippet, as in an item of news.

definitions.meaning: a ... is a ... phone, the British term for a cellphone
A port city on the Gulf coast of Alabama

explanation.surface: A telephone located in an Alabama city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is both the British name for a cellphone and an Alabama port city.

parts.note: a trainer is a sports shoe, the British word for a sneaker

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a spare item of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but a riddle is also a coarse sieve; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle in the gardening sense is a large sieve, one kind of strainer.

clue.text: Following onset of illness, married couple weaken

indicators.note: following says the married-couple letters come after the first one
onset is the start, so the first letter of illness

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: After one falls ill, a husband and wife grow frail.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to damage or diminish, the same as to weaken.

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds the same when spoken, not one spelt the same

parts.note: an outstanding debt is one still owed

explanation.surface: A verse that is said to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' suggests excellent, but here it means unpaid, OWED, which is said the same as ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, often addressed to a subject in praise.

clue.text: Cheese produced by loud Greek character

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheese made by a noisy man from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese from Greece.

definitions.meaning: ... is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, so a Tory is a ...

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who is feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the Conservative Party's colour, and feeling blue means being miserable.

definitions.meaning: the question mark marks the loose sense
saying ... in a quiz means you cannot answer

explanation.surface: Asked whether they will graduate, the student shrugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pass means to succeed in an exam, and is also what a quiz contestant says when stumped.

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Was putting a programme out live a landmark moment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like transmission, but it signals rearranging MADE LIVE; the question mark warns that 'historic' is a loose example.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval means belonging to the Middle Ages, one period of history.

indicators.note: in says the son letter goes inside the club word

parts.note: a union is a club or association

explanation.surface: A boy performs at a club gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concert' looks like a musical show, but here it means agreement, as in acting in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert in the sense of harmony or agreement matches unison, all acting together.

clue.text: Having few worries about a judge appearing heartless

parts.note: C is circa, about

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the central letter is taken out

parts.note: a referee judges a game

explanation.surface: Relaxed about a judge who seems to lack compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing heartless' removes the central E of REFEREE, leaving REFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree describes someone untroubled, free of cares or anxieties.
